\chapter{First order equations}
\section{Integrals as solutions}
\label{sec:integralsols}

\begin{thm}[Picard]
\label{thm:picard}
If $f$ and its partial derivative in $y$ are continuous near $(x_0,y_0)$,
then $y' = f(x,y)$ with $y(x_0) = y_0$ has exactly one solution near $x_0$.
\end{thm}

\begin{example}
The equation $y' = y$ with $y(0) = 1$ satisfies \ref{thm:picard}.
\end{example}

\begin{exercise}[easy]
Solve $y' = 2x$ with $y(0) = 3$.
\end{exercise}
